chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Muhammad al-Wabishi, who said:

Our companions were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so I said, 'I do not have lunch nor dinner except that two or three of them, or fewer or more, are with me.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Their merit upon you is greater than your merit upon them.'

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! How is that, while I feed them my food, spend upon them from my wealth, and my dependents serve them?' He said, 'Indeed, when they come to you, they come with abundant sustenance from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and when they leave, they leave with forgiveness for you.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُنَا: Our companions (referring to the righteous believers or scholars)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of hosting and feeding the righteous companions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia concept of *Ihsan* (beneficence) as a reciprocal spiritual exchange rather than a one-sided charity. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the status of the *Mumin* by framing their presence as a conduit for divine sustenance (*rizq*) and forgiveness, shifting the host's focus from material expenditure to spiritual gain. This perspective reinforces the communal bond where serving the righteous is considered a means of attaining God's pleasure and mercy.
